strings.chrono_subtitle_search: How many countries are you targeting?
strings.chrono_subtitle_flag: How many flags are you targeting?
strings.chrono_subtitle_quiz: How many questions are you targeting?
strings.quiz_find_label: FIND ON MAP → CLICK TO SHOW
strings.info_hint: ↓ Click a country on the map
strings.info_no_data: No data available for this country.
strings.physical_hint: ↓ Click a mountain, river or lake
strings.intro_search_desc: Type a country name in the search box to find it on the map. Found countries are permanently marked in green. Set a timer to play in race mode!
strings.intro_find_desc: A country name appears on screen — click it on the map. Build a streak by answering correctly in a row!
strings.intro_guess_desc: A country is highlighted yellow on the map — type its name and press Enter. Correct and wrong answers are tracked.
strings.intro_info_desc: Click any country to see its name, capital, population, area and world rankings. The capital is marked with a blue dot on the map.
strings.intro_flag_desc: A country's flag is shown — find it on the map and click it. Correct clicks turn the country green and bring a new flag. Play in 5 or 10 minute race mode!
strings.intro_physical_desc: Mountains (▲), rivers (—) and lakes (■) are shown on the map. Click one to see its name, elevation/length/area and a short description.
strings.intro_region_desc: Filter by Europe · Asia · Africa · Americas · Oceania using the scrollable top bar — scroll left!
strings.intro_timer_desc: In Name → Map mode choose 5 / 15 / 20 min for race mode. Quiz modes offer 1 / 2 min speed tests. Results appear when time runs out.
strings.intro_chrono_desc: Click the ⏱ icon on the timer button to activate chronometer mode. Choose your target count of countries / flags / questions (10 / 20 / 30 / 50). The stopwatch starts; when you reach your target, the results screen appears.
strings.intro_streak_desc: In quiz modes your consecutive correct answers build a STREAK. One wrong answer resets it.
strings.intro_map_desc: Drag the map and pinch/scroll to zoom. Current zoom is shown at the bottom right. Double-click to reset view.
strings.intro_share_desc: After a game, tap SHARE to generate a result card with your correct, wrong and streak stats. Share it on social media!
strings.intro_leaderboard_desc: After finishing a timed game in Find on Map, Find Capital, Guess Country, Flag Quiz, Name → Map or Special Taboo, tap the 🏆 LEADERBOARD button. Pick a nickname and submit your score — the highest score is shown at the top. Each mode and each time setting keeps its own table, and your nickname is remembered after the first time.
strings.intro_theme_desc: Click the ☀ / 🌙 button in the top right to switch between light and dark theme.
strings.intro_lang_desc: Available in Turkish, English, German, Chinese, Arabic, Spanish and French. Change language from the top bar.
strings.flag_find_label: Find this country on the map
strings.flag_timed_label: ↓ Find and click this country on the map
strings.intro_capital_desc: A city name is shown on screen — find the country whose capital it is on the map and click it. Correct clicks turn the country green. All timer and streak features from quiz modes apply here too.
strings.intro_tabu_desc: A group game. A word and 5 forbidden words appear on screen. Describe the word to your teammate without using the forbidden words! Categories include countries, geographical features and geography class. In team mode, two teams take turns and compete for points.
strings.tabu_handoff_sub: Pass the phone to the other team!
strings.lb_empty: No scores yet. Be the first!
strings.lb_not_connected: ⚠ Leaderboard not connected yet (missing Firebase config).
strings.koppen_disc_text:
Each country is shown with its dominant climate.
In reality, a country may have multiple climate zones.
strings.cf_subtitle: Discover the leading geographic and economic functions of cities worldwide and in Turkey
strings.cf_hint: ↓ Click a city marker on the map
strings.intro_tabu2_desc: A country-guessing game played solo or as a two-player race. Clues such as continent, flag color and name hint are revealed one by one; you guess and type the country. Easy/Medium/Hard difficulty and question count can be chosen; in duo race mode two players compete on the same questions.
strings.intro_cografya_desc: A gallery of ready-made thematic maps on political, physical, climate, population, economy, disaster and Turkey topics. Filter by category or search; tapping a card opens the large map with its description.
strings.intro_cityfunc_desc: A mode where you discover the leading economic and geographic functions — tourism, industry, trade, port, mining, agriculture and more — of cities worldwide and in Turkey. In Map view, click or hover colored markers to see the info card; in Table view, search and list all cities.

physical_desc.Everest: The highest mountain in the world, located in the Himalayas.
physical_desc.K2: The 2nd highest mountain. Located in the Karakoram range, known as the "Savage Mountain".
physical_desc.Kangchenjunga: The 3rd highest mountain in the world, on the Nepal-India border.
physical_desc.Aconcagua: The highest point in the Western and Southern Hemispheres. Summit of the Andes.
physical_desc.Denali: The highest mountain in North America. Formerly known as McKinley.
physical_desc.Kilimanjaro: The highest point in Africa. The tallest free-standing volcanic mountain in the world.
physical_desc.Elbrus: The highest mountain in Europe, an extinct volcano in the Caucasus.
physical_desc.Mont Blanc: The highest peak in Western Europe, symbol of the Alps.
physical_desc.Ararat: The highest mountain in Turkey, its national symbol. Associated with the legend of Noah's Ark.
physical_desc.Fuji: Japan's iconic dormant volcano, the country's highest point.
physical_desc.Nil: The longest river in the world. Cradle of Egyptian civilization. Flows into the Mediterranean.
physical_desc.Amazon: The world's widest river. Its flow accounts for 20% of all rivers combined.
physical_desc.Yangtze: The longest river in Asia and China. The Three Gorges Dam is built on this river.
physical_desc.Mississippi-Missouri: The main river system of North America, crossing the USA from north to south.
physical_desc.Volga: The longest river in Europe. Of great economic and cultural importance to Russia.
physical_desc.Tuna: The second longest river in Europe, passing through 10 countries.
physical_desc.Fırat: One of the two great rivers of Mesopotamia. Rises in Turkey, flows through Syria and Iraq.
physical_desc.Dicle: One of the two great rivers of Mesopotamia. Rises in Turkish Taurus, flows through Iraq.
physical_desc.Hazar Denizi: The world's largest enclosed body of water, technically a lake with oil reserves.
physical_desc.Baykal Gölü: The world's deepest lake (1,642 m), holding about 20% of the world's fresh water reserves.
physical_desc.Victoria Gölü: Africa's largest lake and the source of the Nile.
physical_desc.Ölü Deniz: The saltiest lake at the lowest point on Earth, 430 m below sea level.
physical_desc.Titicaca Gölü: The largest navigable lake at high altitude, at 3,812 m on the Bolivia-Peru border.
physical_desc.Van Gölü: Turkey's largest lake and one of the world's largest soda lakes, at 1,648 m altitude.
physical_desc.Tuz Gölü: Turkey's second largest lake. Almost no life due to extremely high salt concentration.
physical_desc.Akdeniz: The inland sea bordered by Europe, Africa and Asia. Cradle of ancient civilizations.
physical_desc.Karadeniz: A semi-enclosed sea on Turkey's northern coast. Connects to the Mediterranean via the Straits.
physical_desc.Kızıldeniz: A narrow inland sea between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Connected to the Mediterranean via Suez Canal.
physical_desc.Pasifik Okyanusu: The world's largest and deepest ocean, covering about one third of the Earth's surface.
physical_desc.Atlantik Okyanusu: The world's second largest ocean between Europe-Africa and the Americas.
physical_desc.Hint Okyanusu: The world's third largest ocean, surrounding the Indian subcontinent.
physical_desc.Marmara Denizi: The only inland sea entirely within Turkey's borders. Connects the Black Sea and Mediterranean via the Straits.
physical_desc.Ege Denizi: The sea between Greece and Turkey, home to thousands of islands.
physical_desc.Sahra Çölü: The world's largest hot desert, covering most of North Africa. In some areas annual rainfall is less than 1mm.
physical_desc.Gobi Çölü: Asia's largest desert, spanning Mongolia and China. A cold desert with extreme temperatures. Rich in dinosaur fossils.
physical_desc.Atacama Çölü: The driest desert in the world, on the coast of Chile and Peru. Some stations have never recorded rain.
physical_desc.Namib Çölü: Considered the world's oldest desert (55-80 million years). Famous for giant sand dunes at Sossusvlei.
physical_desc.Antarktika Çölü: The world's largest desert. The entire continent is a desert with extremely low precipitation.
physical_desc.Aden Körfezi: Strategic waterway between the Indian Ocean and Red Sea, known for piracy activities.
physical_desc.Altaylar: Great mountain range of Central/East Asia spanning Russia and Mongolia.
physical_desc.Amur: Forms the natural border between Russia and China; important waterway of the Far East.
physical_desc.Annapurna: The 10th highest mountain. Has the highest fatality rate among 8000-meter peaks.
physical_desc.Aral Gölü: A lake that dramatically shrank due to Soviet irrigation policies — a symbol of ecological disaster.
physical_desc.Arap Denizi: Northwestern extension of the Indian Ocean. Pakistan, India, Oman and Yemen border it. Important trade route.
physical_desc.Balaton: The largest lake in Central Europe, also known as the 'Hungarian Sea'.
physical_desc.Baltık Denizi: Semi-enclosed sea surrounding Northern Europe, with very low salinity compared to the Mediterranean.
physical_desc.Bengal Körfezi: Gulf between India and Myanmar, where monsoon rains are most intense.
physical_desc.Bering Denizi: Sea between Alaska and Russia. During the Ice Age, the land bridge connecting Asia and America was here.
physical_desc.Brahmaputra: Great river originating in Tibet, joining the Ganges in Bangladesh.
physical_desc.Broad Peak: The 12th highest mountain, close to K2 in the Karakoram.
physical_desc.Büyük Ayı Gölü: Canada's largest lake, located within the Arctic Circle.
physical_desc.Cenevre Gölü: The largest Alpine lake in Europe, on whose shore Geneva is situated.
physical_desc.Cho Oyu: The 6th highest mountain. Considered relatively easy among 8000-meter peaks.
physical_desc.Cotapaxi: One of the world's highest active volcanoes, in the Andes of Ecuador.
physical_desc.Demavend: Highest point in the Middle East, an extinct volcano and symbol of Iran.
physical_desc.Dhaulagiri: The 7th highest mountain. Its name means 'White Mountain' in Nepali.
physical_desc.Dinyeper: National symbol of Ukraine. Kyiv was founded on its banks.
physical_desc.Doğu Çin Denizi: Sea between China, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, with important fishing grounds.
physical_desc.Erie Gölü: The shallowest of the Great Lakes. Niagara Falls is fed by this lake.
physical_desc.Etna: Highest active volcano in Europe, located in Sicily, Italy.
physical_desc.Ganj: Sacred river for Hindus and the main water source of India.
physical_desc.Gasherbrum I: The 11th highest mountain in the Karakoram range.
physical_desc.Grossglockner: Highest mountain in Austria, peak of the Austrian Alps.
physical_desc.Güney Okyanusu: Ocean surrounding Antarctica, officially recognized in 2000. Known for strong winds.
physical_desc.Güney Çin Denizi: Strategic sea of Southeast Asia. A significant share of global maritime trade passes through here.
physical_desc.Huang He: China's Yellow River, considered the cradle of Chinese civilization.
physical_desc.Huascarán: Highest mountain in Peru and highest point of the tropical Andes.
physical_desc.Hudson Körfezi: Canada's inland gulf, mostly ice-covered in winter. Home to indigenous hunting communities.
physical_desc.Huron Gölü: Second largest of the Great Lakes, on the US-Canada border.
physical_desc.Hürmüz Körfezi: Most critical chokepoint for global oil trade. About 20% of global oil demand passes through daily.
physical_desc.Issık Göl: Second highest large lake in the world by altitude. The jewel of Kyrgyzstan.
physical_desc.Japon Denizi: Sea between Japan, the Korean Peninsula and Russia. Called 'Sea of Japan' in Japan, 'East Sea' in Korea.
physical_desc.Jungfrau: One of the symbols of the Swiss Alps, home to Europe's highest railway station.
physical_desc.Karayip Denizi: Tropical sea enclosed by Central America, South America and the Antilles. One of the most popular tourist destinations.
physical_desc.Kazbek: Important peak in the Caucasus, associated with the Prometheus legend.
physical_desc.Kenya Dağı: 2nd highest mountain in Africa. The country takes its name from it.
physical_desc.Kolombiya: Important river of North America reaching the Pacific coast.
physical_desc.Kongo: Africa's second longest river and the world's deepest river.
physical_desc.Koralya Denizi: Sea between Australia and Papua New Guinea, home to the Great Barrier Reef.
physical_desc.Kuzey Buz Denizi: Smallest and shallowest ocean, mostly ice-covered year-round. Rapidly melting due to climate change.
physical_desc.Kuzey Denizi: Shallow sea surrounding northwestern Europe, one of Europe's most important oil and gas production areas.
physical_desc.Ladoga Gölü: Largest lake in Europe, near St. Petersburg in Russia.
physical_desc.Lena: Third great river of Siberia, flowing into the Arctic Ocean.
physical_desc.Lhotse: The 4th highest mountain, neighboring Everest in the Himalayas.
physical_desc.Loch Ness: Scotland's famous lake, known worldwide for the 'Nessie' monster legend.
physical_desc.Logan: Highest mountain in Canada, second highest in North America.
physical_desc.Makalu: The 5th highest mountain, known for its distinctive five-sided pyramid shape.
physical_desc.Malawi Gölü: Africa's third largest lake, famous for its extraordinary fish diversity.
physical_desc.Manaslu: The 8th highest mountain. Its name means 'Mountain of the Spirit' in Nepali.
physical_desc.Matterhorn: Iconic pyramid-shaped peak of the Alps on the Swiss-Italian border.
physical_desc.Mekong: Main river of Southeast Asia, flowing through 6 countries.
physical_desc.Meksika Körfezi: Gulf surrounding southern North America, a center for US and Mexican oil production.
physical_desc.Mercan Denizi: Sea where the Great Barrier Reef is located, one of the world's richest areas for biodiversity.
physical_desc.Michigan Gölü: The only Great Lake located entirely within the United States.
physical_desc.Murray-Darling: Australia's longest river system, the main source of water for southeastern Australia.
physical_desc.Nanga Parbat: The 9th highest mountain. Its name means 'Naked Mountain', known for extreme difficulty.
physical_desc.Niger: Longest river in West Africa, known for its unusual inward-flowing course.
physical_desc.Norveç Denizi: Ocean extension west of Norway, with important fisheries and oil reserves.
physical_desc.Ob: Main river of Western Siberia, flowing into the Arctic Ocean.
physical_desc.Ob-İrtiş: Giant river system crossing Siberia, freezing for long periods in winter.
physical_desc.Okhotsk Denizi: Semi-closed sea on Russia's Siberian coast, freezing for most of winter.
physical_desc.Olympos: Home of the gods in Greek mythology. Highest mountain in Greece.
physical_desc.Ontario Gölü: Smallest of the Great Lakes, connected to the Atlantic via the St. Lawrence River.
physical_desc.Orinoco: Main river of Venezuela and Colombia, connected underground to the Amazon.
physical_desc.Pamir: High plateau of Central Asia known as the 'Roof of the World'.
physical_desc.Parana: Second longest river in South America, flowing through Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay.
physical_desc.Puncak Jaya: Highest point in Oceania, has permanent glaciers near the equator.
physical_desc.Ren: Important river of Western Europe, flowing from Switzerland to the North Sea.
physical_desc.Ruwenzori: 3rd highest mountain in Africa, known as the 'Mountains of the Moon'.
physical_desc.Senegal: River forming the border between Senegal and Mauritania.
physical_desc.Superior Gölü: World's largest freshwater lake by surface area. Part of the Great Lakes.
physical_desc.Tanganika Gölü: World's second deepest lake, in the African Rift Valley.
physical_desc.Tasman Denizi: Sea between Australia and New Zealand, known for strong winds and rough waters.
physical_desc.Teide: Highest point in Spain on Tenerife. Active volcano in the Canary Islands.
physical_desc.Tibesti: Highest mountain massif in the Sahara, the roof of central Africa.
physical_desc.Ural: Mountain range separating Europe and Asia, running through Russia.
physical_desc.Urmiye Gölü: Largest lake in the Middle East. Its drying up is a serious ecological problem.
physical_desc.Vesuvius: Active volcano near Naples that destroyed Pompeii in 79 AD.
physical_desc.Vinson: Highest mountain in Antarctica, in the Ellsworth Mountains.
physical_desc.Volta Gölü: Africa's largest artificial lake, created by the Akosombo Dam in Ghana.
physical_desc.Vänern Gölü: Largest lake in Sweden and Western Europe.
physical_desc.Yenisey: The great river of Siberia, flowing into the Arctic Ocean.
physical_desc.Zambezi: Africa's 4th longest river. Victoria Falls is on this river.
physical_desc.Çad Gölü: Lake at the junction of 4 countries, dramatically shrinking due to climate change.
physical_desc.İndus: Main river of Pakistan. The Indus Valley Civilization developed here.
physical_desc.İrlanda Denizi: Sea between England and Ireland, an important maritime route between the two islands.
physical_desc.Arabistan Çölü: Desert covering most of the Arabian Peninsula. Contains the Rub' al Khali, one of the world's largest sand deserts.
physical_desc.Patagonya Çölü: Largest desert in South America, in southern Argentina. Formed in the rain shadow of the Andes.
physical_desc.Büyük Victoria Çölü: Australia's largest desert, in the interior. Covered with sparse shrubs.
physical_desc.Kalahari Çölü: Vast semi-arid region covering southern Africa. Spans Botswana, Namibia and South Africa. Home to diverse wildlife.
physical_desc.Büyük Çöl Havzası: Largest desert in the USA, a high cold desert spanning Nevada, Utah, Idaho and Oregon.
physical_desc.Suriye Çölü: Desert plateau spanning Syria, Iraq, Jordan and Saudi Arabia. Historical Silk Road routes passed through here.
physical_desc.Thar Çölü: Great desert on the Indian subcontinent, on the India-Pakistan border. One of the world's most densely populated deserts.
physical_desc.Kavir Çölü: Iran's great salt desert (Dasht-e Kavir), surrounded by low mountains. Known for salt crusts and marshes.
physical_desc.Lut Çölü: According to NASA data, this Iranian desert has one of the highest surface temperatures on Earth (70.7°C). Features salt flats and rock formations.
physical_desc.Karakum Çölü: Desert covering most of Turkmenistan. Home to the Darvaza 'Gates of Hell' burning gas crater.
physical_desc.Kızılkum Çölü: Desert between Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. Its name means 'red sand' in Turkic.
physical_desc.Taklamakan Çölü: Large desert in China's Xinjiang region. Its Uyghur name means 'once you go in, you can't come out'. Contains important Silk Road routes.
physical_desc.Büyük Sandy Çölü: Desert in northwestern Australia covered with long parallel sand dunes.
physical_desc.Sonora Çölü: Desert in the USA and Mexico, famous for giant saguaro cacti that can live up to 150 years.
physical_desc.Chihuahua Çölü: Largest desert in North America, spanning Mexico and the USA. Major cities like El Paso lie within this desert.
